title: And Still I Rise
author: Maya Angelou
target_audience: Readers of poetry and literary nonfiction
Those interested in civil rights, social justice, and empowerment literature
Students and scholars of African American, women’s, and American literature
core_themes: Resilience in the face of adversity
The enduring power of hope and self-assertion
Identity, pride, and dignity as a Black woman
Overcoming racism, sexism, and social injustice
Transformation of pain into strength and joy
primary_purpose: To celebrate the undying spirit of resilience, hope, and self-worth, particularly from the perspective of a Black woman navigating oppression and prejudice. The poems encourage readers to find strength in their identities and rise above hardship and injustice.

structure_format.narrative_style: Lyric, confessional, and direct, with elements of performance and song
structure_format.organization: Divided into three themed sections, comprising 32 poems of varying lengths
features: Powerful use of repetition and refrain
Imagery rooted in African American history and culture

key_concepts_lessons: Personal resilience can transcend systemic oppression.
Embracing one’s identity and roots fosters empowerment.
Hope and faith in oneself are revolutionary acts.
Art (especially poetry) can be a tool of resistance and healing.
Persistence in the face of adversity is a universal and uplifting message.
notable_features: Inclusion of 'Still I Rise,' one of Angelou’s most famous and anthologized poems
Blends personal and collective experience, linking Angelou’s own story to broader Black and feminist struggles
Accessible yet profound, appealing to a wide readership
Performance-oriented style—many poems are designed to be spoken aloud
cultural_historical_context: Published during the late 1970s, the collection echoes the triumphs and ongoing struggles of the civil rights movement, Black feminism, and the continuing fight for equality. Angelou’s work resonates amid the push for Black cultural pride and the broader feminist movement of the era.
reception_impact: Celebrated as one of Maya Angelou’s most important and inspirational works
Frequently cited in discussions of poetry of resistance and empowerment
Many poems, especially 'Still I Rise,' are widely quoted, recited, and taught
Continues to inspire social movements and personal transformations
Praised for its accessibility, emotional power, and literary artistry
